title: Cooperative reduction by Ln2+ and Cp*− ions: synthesis and properties of Sm, Eu, and Yb complexes with 3,6-di-tert-butyl-o-benzoquinone

synthesis.procedure: All operations were carried out in evacuated vessels or ampoules; compounds were handled in an argon glove-box. Synthesis of 1 was carried out in a two-section ampoule bent at 90°. Solid [Cp*2Sm(thf)2] (0.340 g, 0.602 mmol) and 3,6-di-tert-butyl-o-benzoquinone (0.132 g, 0.600 mmol) were placed in one section. Under cooling with liquid N2, 20 mL of hexane were condensed into the same section and the ampoule was flame-sealed. The mixture was warmed with mixing to room temperature, then stirred at 60 °C for 10 h. After settling of the precipitate, the solution was decanted into the second section. The second section was positioned vertically and heated to ca. 10 °C above room temperature; slow extraction of hexane-soluble components by the temperature gradient afforded yellow crystals of 1 suitable for XRD. Yield 0.233 g (77%).
synthesis.temperature: warmed to room temperature, then 60 °C; crystallization at ca. 10 °C above room temperature

synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: precipitate allowed to settle; solution decanted into the second section; temperature-gradient extraction from hexane gave yellow XRD-quality crystals

properties.summary: Solid-state SQUID data support two weakly coupled or uncoupled Sm(III) centres with catecholate ligands. μeff = 2.17 μB at room temperature, decreasing to 0.48 μB at 2.6 K. Low-temperature variable-field magnetization does not saturate at 2 K up to 5 T.

synthesis.procedure: Prepared analogously to 1 in a two-section ampoule. Solid [Cp*2Yb(thf)] (0.310 g, 0.601 mmol) and 3,6-di-tert-butyl-o-benzoquinone (0.132 g, 0.600 mmol) were combined; 20 mL of hexane were condensed under liquid-N2 cooling and the ampoule was flame-sealed. The mixture was warmed with mixing to room temperature, then stirred at 60 °C for 10 h. After settling, the solution was decanted into the second section and crystals (blue-green for Yb, XRD-quality) grew by temperature-gradient extraction. Yield 0.260 g (82%).

properties.summary: Solid-state μeff at room temperature is 5.48 μB, slightly below the 6.1–6.9 μB range expected for two uncoupled Yb(III) centres, possibly due to impurities or Yb(II)/Yb(III) admixture. μeff decreases to 4.69 μB at 40 K then abruptly to 0.74 μB at 2 K, indicating antiferromagnetic interactions. Magnetization does not saturate at 2 K up to 5 T.

synthesis.procedure: Solid [Cp*2Eu(thf)] (0.130 g, 0.262 mmol) and 3,6-di-tert-butyl-o-benzoquinone (0.057 g, 0.26 mmol) were placed in a Schlenk tube with a Teflon stopper, and 10 mL of toluene were condensed under liquid-N2 cooling. The mixture turned intense blue upon warming, then vinous-red after stirring at room temperature for 1 h. The mixture was stirred overnight and evaporated to dryness. The solids were washed with pentane to remove Cp*2 and extracted with pentane in a bent ampoule analogously to compounds 1 and 2. Red crystals suitable for XRD were separated by decantation. Yield 0.075 g (63%).

properties.summary: Magnetic data support mixed-valent Eu(II)2Eu(III) with catecholate (not ligand-radical) ligands. μeff = 10.98 μB at room temperature, nearly constant from 30–300 K, then rising to 13.21 μB at 2 K, indicating weak ferromagnetic interactions that can be suppressed at H = 5 T. Magnetization saturates at 11–12 NAμB at very low temperature. No ac susceptibility signal, so no slow relaxation/SMM behaviour.
